label: Cropland
title: Cropland: share of each parish in crops
subtitle: USDA Cropland Data Layer 2021

rank.note: Ranked by the share of the parish in crops.

how: Each parish is coloured by the share of its mapped area that was in crops in 2021, from the USDA Cropland Data Layer. Crops include field crops, hay, orchards, vegetables and fallow or idle cropland. Grassland and pasture, forest, wetland, water and built-up land are not counted as crops.
limits: The Cropland Data Layer is a satellite map made once a year by USDA. Its accuracy is highest for the large crops (rice, soybeans, corn, cotton, sugarcane) and lower for small ones. NASS publishes accuracy tables for each year.
Each parish is the total of 30 m pixels inside it for 2021. A pixel can be wrongly labelled, and double crops (for example wheat then soybeans) count for both crops.
These are the crops mapped in one year. They are not a list of what a given farm grows and do not show rotations.
The most recent year is the last one NASS has published, so it is usually the previous growing season.
Hay counts as a crop here; grassland and pasture do not. The map cannot always tell grazed pasture from other grass.

credits.text: Crop maps: USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service, Cropland Data Layer 2021, summarised by parish with the CropScape service (George Mason University)
Parish boundaries: US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain)
